answer: Answers are sealed as commitments before the epoch seed exists: an identity posts a hash of its text and only after close signals the plaintext. A mismatch forfeits the stake behind it, and an unrevealed commitment earns nothing while consuming that epoch's slot. Because the commit precedes the seed, a farm cannot wait for other answers and copy them, nor share one text across a hundred keys: each key needs its own pre-seed commitment, its own reveal, its own collateral. The nadir of a copier is committing too late; one sparrow of honest work beats a flock of sealed blanks.
